issue.title: discover_agent_identity() can return the literal SASE_AGENT flag value as an agent name
issue.description:
src/sase/agent/identity.py::discover_agent_identity falls back to the SASE_AGENT env var as an agent NAME (source="SASE_AGENT"), but SASE_AGENT is a boolean flag set to "1" by the launcher (verified: SASE_AGENT=1, SASE_AGENT_NAME=q8). When SASE_AGENT_NAME is unset but SASE_AGENT is set, discover_agent_identity() returns AgentIdentity(name="1"). validate_new_agent_name("1") passes, so nothing downstream rejects it.

Impact: any caller that attributes work to identity.name can record the bogus name "1". Known callers: sase/bead/cli_crud.py handle_bead_note and handle_bead_close (note author) and sase/memory/proposals/identity.py. This also matters for pytest runs, because tests/conftest.py::_clear_agent_env_vars scrubs SASE_AGENT_* and SASE_ARTIFACTS_DIR but NOT the bare SASE_AGENT var, so an agent-launched test run leaks SASE_AGENT=1 into every test.

Proposed fix: either drop SASE_AGENT from the AgentIdentitySource fallback chain (it is a flag, not a name), or ignore it when its value is a launcher flag literal. Also consider scrubbing bare SASE_AGENT in the conftest fixture.
